subject: A physical Mixer-only Aux name can be changed and read back without adopting an Arrange target
question: Can the bounded name writer use the original Mixer strip's focused editor and verify the committed name on that same source?

reverify.command: In a stopped development fixture, independently observe the existing Aux name, selected Arrange track, Mixer names, routes, faders, playhead and focus. Hold the actual physical Mixer producer's source. Invoke the bounded product channel name writer for a no-op, a stale expected-name refusal, one comma-and-Unicode name change and a fresh exact reverse under the same physical binding. Observe each completed write independently. Do not derive replacement identity from labels or synthesize an owned inverse from a successful scalar receipt.
reverify.expected: The no-op succeeds without a write, stale expected bytes refuse without a write, and the completed writes expose their exact names on the original source. Preserve any playhead or focus movement as an unqualified side effect, not an unchanged preservation footprint.
reverify.cost: Two development-only scalar name writes and their editor acquisition; observations are passive.

method: A development executable linked the actual product module and invoked its channel writer, not a copied native writer or a new public MCP command. The actual producer issued the physical source; its original CF identity was retained across writes and reads. A real mutation claim and operation deadline scoped execution. Independent Accessibility observations compared the exact fixture and before/after UI. The binary contains separate unpublished reader changes and is not a clean publication-head qualification.

canon_not_applicable.reason: The readings concern transient host objects and exact runtime name bytes. Diagnostic labels locate the initial source but do not establish replacement identity or shipped canonical strings.

observations.what: A finite help-free passive observer saw the focused inline editor under the held Aux source
observations.limit: These samples do not prove whole-source continuity during the sampling interval, qualify a writer or isolate the effect of a concurrent UI observation.

observations.what: Actual same-source scalar writes and independent UI readback
Actual injected production-channel failure and correction evidence
observations.limit: Injected tests are not native evidence. The intermediate implementation compile failure is not counted as a runtime RED or a PASS. These seals precede the subsequent independent-review correction.

observations.what: An instrumented repeat on the earlier final source did not reproduce the first playhead drift
observations.limit: Diagnostic wrappers delegated the actual product setter and prepared paired events, with passive reads only after complete pairs. This unchanged repeat neither attributes nor erases the earlier drift.

observations.what: Independent review's finite boundary counterexamples were replayed before correction
observations.counterexamples: A successful late modal census replaced the held window or same-window focused editor before the setter or Return; first-pair completion started transport, opened a sheet or focused a foreign editor before the second pair.
observations.limit: Runtime reproduction was performed separately from the source-only review. Review approval is not inferred from these tests.

observations.what: Fresh safe-focus validation initially refused the native passive strip after one completed click
observations.context_observed: The original physical strip was AXLayoutItem with an insertion point, one original name field and unchanged physical membership. The generic classifier treated this passive container as text editing; the next run refused before any event.
observations.limit: These refusal runs are not successful writes. An intervening diagnostic run also refused before actuation, with raw seal b120330b83241fd2007f51652a64dd077521e2e01c05411360a56acd9a9238b2.

observations.what: A narrowly owned passive-container allowance retained foreign-focus refusals and restored the native scalar roundtrip
observations.limit: The explicit allowance requires the original physical AXLayoutItem, the original unique name field and observed nonsettable value, with final focused-element identity rechecked. Foreign editors and foreign insertion-point containers remain refused. Passive diagnostics can affect timing; this success does not erase the original drift or qualify a clean publication head.

observations.what: Final gesture validation checks physical custody after the passive-focus deciding reads, then checks exact focus before posting
observations.limit: The first harness attempt did not inject the window change and is not credited as a product RED. The corrected children-read hook changed the window during passive-focus qualification and reproduced an extra second pair. Its correction passes without weakening the earlier refusal tests. This final native repeat qualifies only the bounded scalar observation, not an atomic guarantee, owned inverse or whole preservation.

observations.what: The retained focus witness supplies its own classification instead of borrowing another focused object's role
observations.counterexample: After the first pair, the helper captured foreign editable F, the separate classifier lookup returned nonediting W, and the later focus lookup returned F again. The original helper borrowed W's classification and posted the extra second pair.
observations.correction: The shared classifier has a pure retained-element overload. Its original app-focused entry point delegates to the same role/insertion-point logic. The name writer classifies the captured CF object, preserves the original passive-strip allowance and still rechecks final exact focus after physical custody.
observations.limit: This finite failure was runtime-replayed separately from the second source-only review. The repaired witness refuses before the second pair. Prior native success is sealed to the preceding source and is not relabelled as native qualification of this pure classifier correction. No hosted CI, final review approval or whole-issue completion is inferred.

observations.what: Separate existing transport command prepared a display position without qualifying its complete precision
observations.limit: Only bar and beat were observable to the command, so it honestly withheld precise verification. A wrong diagnostic resource URI returned an empty object, not a successful read. Earlier direct UI value attempts returned invalid-element errors. The candidate startup/shutdown reproduced the already-recorded display dependency; none of this establishes a transport or viewport fix.

conclusion: The bounded scalar writer changed and independently read the exact Aux name on its original physical source, then accepted a fresh exact reverse. It did not establish an Arrange association or produce an owned inverse. The observed playhead and focus movement prevents a whole-preservation claim; naming-plan acceptance remains open.
limits: No public command, complete naming adapter, owned inverse, coupled-name preservation or canonical repair plan is qualified by this scalar run.
The playhead moved during the forward interval. Its cause is not isolated and the later unchanged position does not erase that observation.
The measured faders and observed selection/names are a bounded sample, not exhaustive audio-state preservation.
No viewport or focus restoration is claimed; the original focus was not restored.
The observed binary is an unpublished debug candidate and not hosted CI or clean merged-head evidence.
